text:
luca_sales: Hi folks — RapidHealth wants to run a week-long POC calling our private inference endpoint from their hospital cluster. They asked: recommend PrivateLink vs TGW/peering, provide a minimal firewall allowlist (single-line + CIDR), and confirm whether we can offer a single static egress IP for their firewall. Need a short answer for their NetSec team.
nadeem_net: Short answer: PrivateLink for fastest approval; TGW/peering if they need native L3 and preserved client IPs. Static EIP is possible via a dedicated NAT/proxy but it's extra ops + cost.
frank_solutions: For POC we usually push PrivateLink since it avoids route table changes and is scoped to a service. If RapidHealth wants full visibility of client IPs in our logs, TGW/peering or a proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For is needed.
tara_sec: Security checklist: 1) Confirm whether they do TLS interception. If yes, cert pinning or mTLS might fail. 2) Request VPC Flow Logs on endpoint subnets for audit. 3) If we provide a dedicated EIP, it must be single-tenant for regulated customers.
luca_sales: They only allow outbound 443 from the hospital cluster. Is that okay?
nadeem_net: Yes. Both PrivateLink and TGW peering are compatible with 443/tcp. If we provision a proxy with an EIP, their firewall will point to that EIP:443.
frank_solutions: Minimal allowlist snippet to paste into their ticket (one-line + CIDR example):
```
# One-line (single example IP for EIP flow): allow tcp from 10.200.0.0/22 to 54.210.99.11 port 443  # replace with actual EIP
```
```
# CIDR example (for Interface Endpoint ENIs): allow tcp from 10.200.0.0/22 to 10.240.16.0/28 port 443  # replace with endpoint ENI CIDR
```
tara_sec: Add the following to the ticket: enable VPC Flow Logs on the endpoint subnets and share flow log S3/CloudWatch path for audit. Also, confirm whether they need mTLS for the POC.
nadeem_net: Operational notes: 1) Interface endpoints create ENIs in each AZ used by the endpoint; confirm subnet IP capacity and ENI quota. 2) ENI IPs can change if endpoint is replaced; we usually publish the exact ENI IPs after provisioning. 3) MTU: proxies/inspection can reduce MTU and break long streaming sessions — recommend streaming test.
luca_sales: Quick POC pricing delta — can you give a ballpark to include in the SOW?
frank_solutions: Ballpark (POC-size): PrivateLink: cloud provider charges ~ $0.01-$0.12/hr per endpoint + $0.01-$0.05/GB processed (varies by region) — customer typically covers cloud fees; we add a small per-GB handling surcharge if we host a proxy. TGW/peering: usually lower per-GB for sustained heavy use but higher setup/approval time. Dedicated EIP/proxy: one-time setup fee (~$250-$500) + monthly infra (~$50-$200) + per-GB handling. These are estimates; final quote after region confirmation.
ops-bot: Ticket created: POC-7032 assigned to @frank_solutions for endpoint + EIP quote. ETA 48 hours.
tara_sec: Also note DNS behavior: with PrivateLink, the private DNS name will resolve to endpoint IPs in their VPC if private DNS is enabled; if they use hard-coded host allowlists, provide ENI CIDRs. If they rely on FQDN-only allowlisting, confirm outbound proxy behavior.
nadeem_net: If they need preserved source IPs for audit and choose PrivateLink, we can ask them to run a small forwarding proxy that injects X-Forwarded-For into requests, but that changes trust model.
luca_sales: Can someone draft 3 quick bullets I can email RapidHealth? Keep it short.
frank_solutions: Email bullets: 
- PrivateLink (recommended for POC): fastest security approval, minimal routing changes, customer creates interface endpoint and allowlists ENI IPs or uses our published endpoint list.
- Transit GW / VPC Peering: full L3 connectivity and preserves client source IPs; better for long-term integrations but requires network change windows and route updates.
- Dedicated EIP / Proxy: single-IP allowlist option for strict firewalls; requires provisioning, infra/setup fee, and dedicated EIP (single-tenant if required).
ops-bot: Reminder: please confirm cloud provider + region, whether RapidHealth accepts ENI CIDR allowlist or requires single EIP, and whether TLS inspection is in-scope. We'll provide exact ENI IPs / EIP quote after ticket kickoff.
luca_sales: Great — I'll send this and ask for region today. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
